extracted.intended_audience: contributors/maintainers of the Lean (mathlib) library (Lean 3 era)
extracted.subtask_description: Coding and documentation style guidelines for files in the Lean (mathlib) library, covering naming, file headers, docstrings, formatting of declarations/proofs, tactic style, and documentation practices. Targeted at authors editing or contributing Lean library files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred names for various syntactic/semantic categories of variables (universes, types, propositions, elements, assumptions, predicates/relations, lists, sets, naturals, integers) and conventions for types with mathematical content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use u, v, w, ... for universes; α, β, γ, ... for generic types; a, b, c, ... for propositions; x, y, z, ... for elements of a generic type; h, h₁, ... for assumptions; p, q, r, ... for predicates and relations; s, t, ... for lists; s, t, ... for sets; m, n, k, ... for natural numbers; i, j, k, ... for integers. Types with mathematical content are expressed with usual mathematical notation (G for a group, R for a ring, K or 𝕜 for a field, E for a vector space, ...). Older files may use greek letters for all types; pull requests renaming type variables in these files are welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line length
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit line length to improve readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lines should not be longer than 100 characters (helps reading on small screens/windows).

rubrics_metrics.name: File header content
rubrics_metrics.description: Every file should start with a copyright header and metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The file header should contain copyright information, a list of all the authors who have made significant contributions to the file, and a description of the contents. Example header shown (copyright, license, Author).

rubrics_metrics.name: Imports placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where and how to put imports in a file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do all imports right after the header, without a line break, on separate lines (i.e., header, then immediately import lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors list guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: How to decide who to list as authors in the header.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No strict rules on what contributions qualify; general idea: people listed should be those you'd reach out to with questions about the design or development of the Lean code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module docstring requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Module-level documentation expected after header and imports (delimited with /-! and -/).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a title of the file, a summary of contents (main definitions and theorems, proof techniques), notation used in the file (if any), references to literature (if any). Use sections (e.g., ## Main results, ## Notation, ## References). Add new bibliography entries to docs/references.bib. See documentation requirements for more suggestions and examples. A template/example module docstring is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spaces around punctuation and operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Spacing conventions around colons, ':=', and infix operators and where to place them relative to line breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use spaces around ':', ':=' or infix operators. Put them before a line break rather than at the beginning of the next line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation width
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred indentation amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use two spaces to indent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof first-line alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: How the first line of a proof should be aligned relative to the theorem statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After stating the theorem, generally do not indent the first line of a proof so that the proof is 'flush left' in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-line theorem statement indentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indentation rules when theorem/type lines wrap across multiple lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the theorem statement requires multiple lines, indent the subsequent lines (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arguments in proof terms formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format proof terms that take multiple arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a proof term takes multiple arguments, it can be clearer (and often necessary) to put some of the arguments on subsequent lines; indent each argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid orphan parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Parentheses should stay with their arguments rather than being left dangling on a line by themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't orphan parentheses; keep them with their arguments (example shows keeping parentheses with the text they group).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short declarations on a single line
rubrics_metrics.description: When short declarations can be compacted to one line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short declaration can be written on a single line (examples: short lemma, short def).

rubrics_metrics.name: 'have' / 'from' pair formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting rules for have ... , from ... constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A have/from pair can be on the same line (have H2 : ..., from subst ...). You can also put 'from' on the next line if the justification is long. If the justification takes more than a single line, keep the 'from' on the same line as the 'have', and then begin the justification indented on the next line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indent additional lines of long arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: When arguments themselves require line breaks, how to indent continuation lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the arguments themselves are long enough to require line breaks, use an additional indent for every line after the first (example given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class/structure field indentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indentation rules for fields inside class or structure definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a class or structure definition, do not indent fields (example shows fields aligned without extra indentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructor argument alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: How to align arguments when using a constructor with several arguments in a definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using a constructor taking several arguments in a definition, arguments line up vertically (example given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instance definitions formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting conventions for instance declarations involving braces and ':='.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When defining instances, opening and closing braces are not alone on their line. The content is indented by two spaces and ':=' lines up (example provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypotheses left of colon
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer putting arguments/hypotheses to the left of the colon rather than using universal quantifiers/implications when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally preferred when the proof starts by introducing these variables. Examples: prefer example (n : ℝ) (h : 1 < n) : 0 < n := by linarith over example (n : ℝ) : 1 < n → 0 < n := λ h, by linarith. Explanation and examples given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binder spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Spacing after binders in quantifiers/forall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a space after binders: example : ∀ α : Type, ∀ x : α, ∃ y, y = x := λ (α : Type) (x : α), exists.intro x rfl.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculational proofs alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write calculational proofs neatly and when to compact them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It looks nice when the comparisons and justifications line up neatly. To be more compact, you may align only after the first line (examples given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactic block indentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indentation rules when opening a tactic block (begin ... end).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When opening a tactic block, 'begin' is not indented but everything inside is indented (example given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed term/tactic mode examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and examples for mixing term-mode and tactic-mode proofs cleanly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate how to combine le_antisymm style term proofs with begin ... end blocks, showing indentation and rw/simp usage; follow the general tactic-block indentation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focusing braces for side-condition goals
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format new goals that arise as side conditions or steps within tactic blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When new goals arise as side conditions or steps, enclose them in focusing braces and indent (except possibly the last goal if much longer). Braces are not alone on their line (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional trailing comma in tactic blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the final step in a begin ... end block may be followed by a comma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final step may be followed by a comma, but there is no style rule requiring it. Many prefer it (infoview display), others dislike it; both styles exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of semicolon and sequencing tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Cautions and preferred patterns when sequencing tactics with ';' or using by ... versus begin ... end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: t0; t1 is used to execute t0 then t1 on all new goals, but ';' is not a comma: either write tactics in one line or indent the following tactic. For single-line tactic proofs (or short tactic proofs embedded in a term), prefer 'by ...' rather than 'begin ... end'. If using multiple tactics inside a 'by ...' block, use braces: by { tac1, tac2 } rather than abusing ';'. Put a single tactic invocation per line unless you are closing a goal with a proof that fits entirely on a single line. Short sequences of tactics corresponding to a single mathematical idea can be on a single line (examples: cases bla, clear h). Use swap or work_on_goal to close very short goals to avoid extra indentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blank line separation of declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use blank lines between theorems and definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally use a blank line to separate theorems and definitions, but this can be omitted to group together a number of short definitions or to group a definition and notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal forms (canonical statement forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick and use a normal form for equivalent statements to ensure consistency and usability (e.g., for dot-notation and simp rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set a normal form and use it in statements and conclusions. Examples: prefer s.nonempty (for dot notation) and (a : option α) instead of some a. Often register simp lemmas to convert other forms to the normal form. Special case: in types with bottom/top, prefer hne (x ≠ ⊥) in assumptions (easier to check) and hlt (⊥ < x) in conclusions (more powerful to use). Note natural example where ⊥ = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment style
rubrics_metrics.description: Which comment delimiters to use in which contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use module doc delimiters '/-! -/' to provide section headers and separators (these appear in generated docs). Use '/- -/' for technical comments or implementation notes or comments in proofs. Use '--' for short or inline comments. Documentation strings for declarations are delimited with '/-- -/'. See documentation requirements for more suggestions and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography additions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where to add new bibliography entries referenced from module docstrings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New bibliography entries should be added to docs/references.bib.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor convenience: header skeleton
rubrics_metrics.description: A tip for quickly generating the file header skeleton in VS Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you're editing mathlib in VS Code, you can write 'copy' and then press TAB to generate a skeleton of the copyright header.
